svg.text: Barriers vs builders: choose your wall

g.text: BARRIERS (knock down!)
jargon · rushing · judging ·
noise · pain · fear · language
BUILDERS (build up!)
plain words · sitting ·
privacy · humour · hope
NON-VERBAL 70%
face + eyes + posture +
touch speak first!
CONGRUENCE
words + face + tone
must MATCH!
AUDIT EVERY CONTACT: which barriers are up? (standing over bed? shouting over noise?
English to a Twi-only elder?) — knock ONE down before clinical talk. Builders cost nothing:
a chair, a curtain, a greeting in THEIR language, unhurried eyes.
NON-VERBAL DOMINATES: face (warmth/worry leak!), eyes (attention vs screen-staring!),
posture (lean in, uncross!), gestures (open palms!), touch (hand on forearm = courage —
ask culture + consent!), space (bedside-close, not towering!), time (sitting = "you matter").
CONGRUENCE: "I'm listening" + eyes on phone = LIE patients believe over words. Match face +
tone + words, always. Incongruence destroys trust faster than silence.
GHANA REALITIES: 80+ languages (learn greetings! use interpreters, never children for bad
news!); communal decisions (family meetings, elder respect!); spiritual framing ("by God's
grace" + medicine, not versus!); hierarchy (kneel/greet elders properly!). Exam gold.
PATIENT-SIDE BARRIERS: pain (treat FIRST, talk after!), fear, shame (STI? fistula? mental
illness?), low literacy (pictures + teach-back!), deafness (face + write!), denial. Meet the
barrier before the message — unheard messages are unspoken ones.
NURSE-SIDE BARRIERS: rushing ("I have 40 patients" shows!), jargon ("hypertension" → "BP
high — blood pushing too hard!"), assumptions ("illiterate = unintelligent" — NEVER!),
fatigue, prejudice. Check yourself at the curtain.
MANTRA: "sit, greet, curtain, plain words — then clinical talk."
